item.title: The Duplicate
item.author: techjourneyman@gmail.com (techjourneyman)
item.description: The thin handles of the plastic grocery bag dug painfully into my fingers, carrying nothing more than a cheap box of coffee filters. Ten minutes. I had been gone for ten minutes. Yet as I pushed open the front door, the air inside felt instantly, terrifyingly wrong. The deadbolt was unlatched. From the kitchen, the familiar sizzle of searing garlic drifted down the hallway, wrapped in the warm, careless laughter of my wife and daughter.

item.title: The 30 Second Polaroid
item.author: techjourneyman@gmail.com (techjourneyman)
item.description:
The 30-Second Polaroid

Arthur bought the vintage Polaroid camera from a dusty estate sale for fifteen bucks. The seller—a twitchy old woman who smelled faintly of copper—insisted it was “already loaded” and refused to take a penny more.

When Arthur got back to his apartment, he aimed it at his kitchen island and pressed the shutter. The camera whirred, spitting out a blank square of film. As the colors slowly bloomed, Arthur frowned. In the photo, a red ceramic mug sat shattered on the tile floor.
